questions.q: What should MissedOpportunities::canViewCardData() return for an UNAUTHENTICATED caller -- true or false?
questions.answer: Return FALSE for a guest. Implement canViewCardData() as auth()->check() && (Feature::active(FeatureEnum::MISSED_OPPORTUNITY->slug()) || session()->has('admin_impersonator')). This requires editing the Company Metrics foundation's guest-parity test test_can_view_card_data_is_total_with_no_authenticated_user(): keep its stated purpose (prove expandableCards() is callable with no authenticated user WITHOUT erroring) and relax the incidental cards()==expandableCards() key-equality assertion, which no longer holds now that a real gate drops the key via array_filter.
questions.why_it_is_not_code_derivable: Both answers are safe and both are defensible; they differ in intended behaviour, not correctness. Pennant does not throw either way (S13). No guest ever renders the dashboard regardless -- Dashboard::mount() aborts unless the viewer holds ADMIN or USER. So this is about (a) which existing regression test changes and (b) whether expandableCards()'s array SHAPE should reveal Pro-gating to an unauthenticated caller.

options.label: Return true for a guest (guard with auth()->guest() first)
options.consequence: the Company Metrics foundation's guest-parity test test_can_view_card_data_is_total_with_no_authenticated_user() stays green UNTOUCHED. Matches the DashboardMetricCard interface docblock's literal wording that the default 'MUST be total with NO authenticated user'. Slightly odd semantically: a guest nominally 'may see' a Pro metric.

options.label: Return false for a guest (auth()->check() && (Feature::active(...) || impersonator))
options.consequence: Semantically cleaner and is what the closed reference implementation shipped. But it requires editing that guest-parity regression test, because expandableCards() is an array_filter that DROPS the gated key, so cards() and expandableCards() keys stop matching for a guest.

questions.driver_recommendation: Option 2 (return false for a guest). The guest test's STATED purpose, in its own comment, is that 'the default must not dereference auth()->user()' -- i.e. it guards against ERRORING, and the key-equality assertion is merely the mechanism it used to prove callability. Option 2 preserves that purpose while relaxing an incidental assertion, and the Company Metrics foundation already explicitly authorised this ticket to update its gating expectations. Option 1 keeps the diff marginally smaller but encodes a claim ('a guest may view this Pro metric') that will read as wrong to the next person.

questions.q: Does this ticket wire MissedOpportunityClientGraph up as the card's expanded detail, or just fix its grain bug where it sits?
questions.answer: FIX IN PLACE. Do NOT wire MissedOpportunityClientGraph into any page or into the card-expansion path. Do NOT touch app/Filament/Pages/Dashboard.php. Do NOT change the graph's hardcoded year-to-date window. Scope stays the 8 planned files. AC-3 is read as: the grain fix lands, and the CARD's compact and expanded views agree by construction (same class, same query). The graph remains orphaned and the grain fix is a latent correctness fix with no user-visible effect today -- this MUST be stated plainly in the Build Record so it is not mistaken for a shipped user-facing fix.
questions.materiality: MATERIAL (scope, and an AC that is not achievable as literally written)
questions.why_it_is_not_code_derivable: The ticket asserts 'That chart is the expanded detail behind this card.' Three verified facts contradict that: (S15) the graph is wired to nothing at all; (S14) a card's expanded view is structurally THE SAME CLASS re-rendered at 600px, so no different class can serve a key's expanded view without changing Dashboard; and (S16) the graph's window is hardcoded year-to-date, not the page filter. So AC-3's 'agrees with the compact card for the same window' cannot hold literally.

options.label: Fix in place; leave it orphaned
options.consequence: Matches the current architecture and what the reference implementation did (its own prep artifacts call the graph 'a query-logic reuse candidate, NOT a drop-in card and NOT something to wire in instead of the new card'). AC-3 is then satisfied by construction for the CARD (its compact and expanded views are the same class and query, so they cannot disagree), and the grain fix is banked as a latent correctness fix. HONEST COST: the grain fix has no user-visible effect, because nobody can reach the graph.
options.changes: The 8 files above. Roughly a half-day.

options.label: Also wire the graph up so it is genuinely the expanded detail
options.consequence: Delivers what the ticket's prose describes, and makes the grain fix actually visible to users. But it is materially more work and touches the Company Metrics foundation's shared expansion machinery: Dashboard would need to support a second class per key (or the per-client breakdown would need folding into MissedOpportunities' own expanded rendering), AND the graph would need to stop being hardcoded YTD and start honouring the page filter -- otherwise AC-3 still fails.
options.changes: The 8 files PLUS app/Filament/Pages/Dashboard.php (shared, foundation-owned) and a rewrite of the graph's windowing. Meaningfully larger, and it re-opens a file nine sibling tickets depend on.

questions.driver_recommendation: Option 1 (fix in place). It is what the architecture supports, what the reference implementation concluded after nine review rounds, and it keeps the Company Metrics foundation's shared expansion code untouched for the eight sibling tickets still to come. If you want the per-client breakdown to be reachable, that is a cleaner separate ticket than a rider on this one. I would take Option 1 and note the orphan status explicitly in the Build Record so it is not forgotten.

notes: TEST-RUN TRAP (knowledge card clarity/testing.md): `php artisan test` cannot run the full suite locally -- at the default memory_limit it OOMs during DISCOVERY and STILL EXITS 0, reporting a false pass. CH TEST DB TRAP (same card): tests/Concerns/RequiresClickhouse TRUNCATEs a HARDCODED clarity.*/zod.* list, so local ClickHouse test databases must use the LITERAL names clarity and zod. And .env.testing with CLICKHOUSE_DRIVER=pgsql makes RequiresClickhouse skip EVERY ClickHouse test while reporting all-green -- if a CH suite looks suspiciously fast or unanimously green, check the driver first.
